transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because I just can’t seem to stop launching projects. It's like I'm constantly starting new things—massive work plans, new certification schedules, completely upgrading my home network, sending out messages to a bunch of old contacts. It just gets so intense, and I blow way past normal limits. Honestly, I don't really stop until my wife or my director at work finally has to step in and tell me to dial it back.
Have you noticed needing less sleep than usual when you're in these intense periods of starting new projects?

Yeah, definitely. There have been runs where I sleep maybe three hours. I'll just wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m., and... instead of feeling tired, it honestly just feels like I’ve been handed bonus time. I just get right back to whatever I was working on.
When you're in these high-energy periods, how do you feel emotionally? Are you unusually upbeat, confident, or maybe even irritable?

It's kind of a mix, honestly. Some weeks I feel... I don't know, almost electric. Like I'm just completely unstoppable. But at the same time, if there's even a tiny delay with something I'm working on, or if my wife just asks a simple question, I can just snap. It gets really frustrating because in those moments, it honestly feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite when you're in these high-energy periods?

Yeah, my eating definitely goes off track. It kind of goes in both directions, depending on how I'm doing. When I'm in one of those really driven periods, I just... I forget to eat meals entirely. I pretty much just live on coffee to keep going. But then, when I hit those low periods, I end up snacking a lot, especially late at night, and I'll notice my weight starts creeping up.
Have you had periods where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, especially after these high-energy times?

Yeah, I do. There are these stretches where I'll just... I wake up feeling like a completely failed version of myself. I just feel heavy and flat all day. When it gets like that, honestly, even just answering my wife’s normal questions feels like it's too much to handle.
How long do these down or depressed periods usually last when you're feeling heavy and flat most of the day?
They last a while. If I look back over this whole thing, I'd say those low, withdrawn periods have added up to about seven months in total. It's just a long time to feel that way.
How long does a typical depressed period last from start to finish?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. It's hard to pin down exactly when one starts and when it finally lifts. It just feels like it drags on for weeks at a time, but I haven't really kept track of a specific number of days or anything.
Can you recall if any of those depressed periods lasted at least two weeks without letting up?

I'm really not sure. Um, it's hard to say if it was a full two weeks straight without any kind of break. Like I mentioned, it just feels like they drag on for a while, but I never marked it on a calendar to see if it hit that two-week mark exactly.
Looking back, can you confirm if there was ever a time when you felt down or hopeless nearly every day, and that period lasted for at least two full weeks without any real break?

Yeah, I guess if I really think about it... yes. There are these stretches where I just wake up feeling like a failed version of myself. It's just this heavy, flat feeling that stays with me all day, every day. It gets to the point where even answering my wife's normal, everyday questions just feels like too much effort. And those stretches, they definitely go on for at least two weeks straight without any real break.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was extremely elevated, expansive, or irritable, and you had more energy or activity than usual that lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Yeah, I have. Some weeks I feel almost... electric, I guess. Like I'm completely unstoppable and have all this energy. But during those same times, if there's even a tiny delay in something, or if my wife just asks me a simple question, I can snap. It's like I get so irritated, almost like everyone around me is trying to slow me down on purpose. And yeah, those periods definitely last for more than four days at a time.
Have you had three or more separate manic periods in your lifetime?
I don't think so. I mean, I've had those electric stretches a few times, but I really couldn't tell you if it's been three separate times or more. I just know it's happened.
Can you recall if any of those high-energy, electric periods lasted for a full week or more without letting up?

I don't really know if they lasted a full week. I mean, they definitely go on for a few days, like I said, but I haven't really kept track of exactly how many days they last. It's hard to say for sure if it was a whole seven days straight.
Can you confirm if any of those high-energy, electric periods lasted for at least a full week without letting up?

Like I said before, I really haven't kept track of the exact number of days. I just know that during those times, I feel completely electric and unstoppable. But at the same time, the smallest thing—like a minor delay or my wife just asking me a question—makes me snap. It just feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down. But as for it being exactly seven days, I just can't say for sure.
Can you confirm if any of those high-energy, electric periods lasted for at least 7 full days without letting up, even if you didn't track it exactly at the time?

I honestly don't know. I mean, I get what you're asking, but I just don't have a clear memory of the exact timeline. It's not something I was measuring while it was happening. I just know it goes on for days, but I really can't confirm if it hit that seven-day mark.
Looking back as best as you can recall, was there ever a time when you felt that electric, high-energy mood for seven days in a row or more without it letting up?
Doc, I feel like we're going in circles here. I really just don't know. I can't give you a yes or a no on it being exactly seven days. It just wasn't something I was keeping track of.
Looking back as best you can, can you recall if there was ever a time when you felt that high-energy, electric mood for a full week or more without it letting up at all?

I... I really don't know how else to say this. I just don't know. I can't remember if it was a full week or not. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just genuinely don't have an answer for you on the exact number of days.
Looking back, can you clearly recall if there was ever one stretch where you felt that electric, high-energy mood every single day without it letting up at all for a full week or more?

Look, I know I just said I can't be sure about the exact number of days, but... if you mean a full week where I just felt completely different, then yeah, some weeks I do feel almost electric and unstoppable. Like I can do anything. But then, during those same stretches, if there's even a tiny delay or my wife asks me a simple question, I just snap. It feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. So, yes, there are whole weeks like that.
Looking back, was there ever a time when you felt that electric, high-energy mood every single day without it letting up at all for a full week or more?

I mean, like I just said a second ago... yes. There definitely are whole weeks like that. I get this feeling where I'm just electric and completely unstoppable. But at the same time, if my wife asks me a simple question or if there's even a tiny delay with something, I just snap. It feels like everyone around me is dragging their feet on purpose just to slow me down. So, yeah, I have had full weeks of feeling exactly like that.
Looking back, was there ever a time when you felt that electric, high-energy mood every single day without it letting up at all for a full week or more?

Doc, I feel like we're just repeating ourselves now. Yes. Like I've been telling you, there have been full weeks where it doesn't let up. I'll have that electric, completely unstoppable energy for seven days straight, or more. 

But like I mentioned, it's not just good energy. If my wife asks me something, or if there's even a small delay with anything, I snap. I get so angry because it feels like people are purposely trying to slow me down. So, yes, a full week or more of exactly that.
